Control coded public with medium confidence: UA was created by Flemish decree (1995/2003) with legal personality and no private founder or owner, and is supervised by a Flemish Government commissioner; but the decree does not call it an 'openbare instelling' (unlike Ghent), KBO records 'Andere rechtsvorm', and the board is mostly elected internally with 3 externally appointed seats (1 by the education minister, 1 by the provincial governor, 1 by the Jesuit provincial, a legacy of the 2003 merger with the Jesuit UFSIA). Checker V015 read the decree (art. 7): of 28 board seats, 4 are ex officio, 16 elected by staff and students, 1 named by the education minister, 1 by the provincial governor, 1 by the Jesuit provincial and 6 co-opted. There is no state-appointed majority, but no private owner or appointing body either (the Jesuit seat is 1 of 28). For public: the legislature itself fixes the board composition (not a private organising authority as at KU Leuven/UCLouvain); UA is the general legal successor of RUCA (state university centre) and UIA and received their assets by operation of law (Decr. 4 Apr 2003 art. 10, 21); KBO registers UA's activity as 'Officieel hoger onderwijs' (NACE 2003: 'Hoger onderwijs ingericht door de Gemeenschappen'), the same class as Ghent, whereas KU Leuven is 'Vrij gesubsidieerd hoger onderwijs'. Against: Codex III.58 calls Ghent a 'publiekrechtelijke instelling' and groups UA with KU Leuven, VUB and UHasselt for employer-cost compensation, and the UA decree does not use 'openbare instelling'. Public kept (state creation and official education network, as for Ghent and the GRC/POL/ROU precedent). Belgium's control type (2/5 public = mixed vs 1/5 = private) depends on this row; report it as a sensitivity. If treated as private it would be private_nonprofit with govt_dependent yes. Govt aid: studietoelage plus reduced fees (bijna-beurstarief if income is at most EUR 3,768 above the grant ceiling in 2023/24). Inst aid: Sociale Dienst 'sociale toelage' after a social and financial investigation (2023/24 capture).

notes: Control private_nonprofit (strict test): the Knesset Research and Information Center (2018) states that a university recognised under s.14 of the Council for Higher Education Law 1958 'is not a statutory corporation but a private body enjoying full institutional autonomy' (quasi-public status noted); TAU is incorporated under s.14 of the CHE Law only. No state ownership found. Governing bodies under the CHE-binding Grossman principles (2004): the Board of Governors (supreme body) consists of Israeli and overseas persons with an interest in the institution; public members of the Executive Committee are chosen by a search committee drawn from the Executive Committee itself - no government appointment of a governing-body majority found (checker V015 read the TAU Constitution: the Board of Governors is 'a self governing body'. Its Israeli non-academic members are elected by the Board itself, and up to a quarter of Israeli members are elected by the Senate. The 13-member Executive Council is the chair, president, rector, 3 Senate appointees and 7 public representatives: 2 appointed by the Board of Governors Standing Committee and 5 elected by the Executive Council from a search-committee list. There is no government appointee). govt_dependent_flag yes: the PBC (VATAT) budgets the university's teaching component as number of students x tariff by field and degree x efficiency coefficient (PBC budget model, 2012 document, nearest year), and the government funds the national reduction of first-degree tuition (TAU note: the reduction 'is based on the government's commitment to fund this reduction'). Charge: TAU 2023/24 basic first-degree tuition NIS 11,264 for a 100% annual load (the CHE-set reduced rate; the reduction is conditional on registering for and passing at least 18 credit hours in the year - met by the baseline full-time student, otherwise the unreduced rate applies); fees = security fee 610 (compulsory) + national representative student organisation 10 (statutory, CHE rules 2018) = 620. Welfare fee NIS 367 excluded: students may opt out in advance (sensitivity with it: 12,251). Note TAU's page shows 11,264 while HUJI/Technion/BGU/BIU show the national rate 11,296 at the July-2023 index (TAU states its figure at the June-2023 index, 'not less than' the July-index amount) - difference NIS 32, not band-relevant. Engineering/law take more years (more total %), not a higher annual rate; overhead/drag charges apply only outside the standard path. govt_need_aid targeted (national scheme cited by rule): PBC/CHE Student Aid Fund (keren ha-siyua, Ministry of Education-CHE; 'Mil-GO' scholarship) - grants for first-degree students scored on per-capita household income (40% weight) and other criteria, four tiers NIS 5,000-12,480, at least 4,000 recipients a year (criteria decided 16.3.22; operated by Perach/Davidson from 2022/23; no 2023/24-specific call read, so year = nearest documented). Ministry of Defense discharged-soldier study grants are not means-tested and Perach is service-linked - not coded. Loans excluded. inst_need_aid targeted: TAU Dean of Students financial-aid scholarships awarded on the economic situation of the student and family relative to other applicants, from 10% of annual tuition up to full tuition; recipient share not documented.

No general national government means-tested grant found; กยศ. loans excluded. inst_fee_aid yes: CMU central scholarship (ทุนส่วนกลางมหาวิทยาลัยเชียงใหม่), funded from university budget and donations, 10,000-50,000 THB/yr allocated by degree of financial need (current page); faculties also award about 1,500 scholarships/yr. inst_cash_aid unknown (no source seen stating money is paid to the student).
